newsitem.title: UK: Rangebound gold gets mild boost from stocks.
newsitem.headline: Rangebound gold gets mild boost from stocks.

text.p: Gold prices were slightly firmer on Monday after Friday's sharp fall in the U.S. stock market, but Wall Street's woes failed to lift bullion from its tight range.
"People aren't rushing in. They want to see whether the situation with the stock market continues or was just a one-off," a dealer said, referring to the Dow's near-250 point plunge last week.
Gold was fixed at $326.05 an ounce, compared to $324.65 on Friday afternoon and a high around $327.00 overnight.
Dealers said prices were still firmly esconced in a broader $320-$330 range, with interim support at $325.
On the charts gold was looking increasingly bearish after failing to break higher, technical analysts said.
Any upside potential from short covering by funds was being countered by producer selling, dealers and analysts said.
Underhedged producers are panicking with gold at 12-year lows and taking advantage of even small rallies to sell forward.
"There are lots of issues out there - central banks, producer selling, the stock market and what will happen with interest rates," a dealer said.
"If we do get a rate rise you'll see gold down on producer selling rather than a rise on the back of a stock exchange fall."
Business was muted in early Europe, particularly with the Hong Kong market closed. The market was holding its breath until the U.S. stock market resumed business.
In the other precious metals, silver was higher after a fund-led rally on Friday whisked prices firmly above $4.50 an ounce.
It was last indicated at $4.53/$4.55, up nine cents. But in the near term silver was seen consolidating or falling back.
"On Friday three funds that sold it down previously bought it back," a dealer said.
"But Friday is not the best day to cover your shorts as trade is thin so we'll probably see it pressured down to 450 - the middle of the recent range."
The platinum group metals (PGMs) were slightly firmer although well within recent price ranges, with palladium still hovering around the $210 support level.
Platinum was last indicated $2.50 firmer at $425.50/$428.50, while palladium was $210.00/$213.00, up $3.00.
